plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The question asks which genes and which hallmark pathways change between treated (AD lesional) and control skin, with care around the shallow sample sample_01. The data are raw integer gene-level counts from Salmon (12000 genes x 12 samples; 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch). The pipeline: (1) sample-structure QC on blind variance-stabilized values (PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) that inspects and reports sample_01 (~4x below median depth) instead of silently dropping it, since size factors down-weight depth and removal needs a stated reason; (2) a single PyDESeq2 run - minimal pre-filter (10 counts in at least 6 samples), median-of-ratios size factors inside the NB GLM, Wald test of condition treated vs control with an explicit control reference level, apeglm-style LFC shrinkage, BH FDR at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering - because the user requires Python for every script and PyDESeq2 0.5.4 implements the recommended DESeq2 procedure; (3) a leave-one-out sensitivity rerun without sample_01 that quantifies its influence on the gene list so the keep-or-drop decision is evidence-based; (4) preranked GSEA of all tested genes ranked by the Wald statistic (the stated choice among the disputed rank metrics) against the MSigDB human hallmark collection (50 sets, HGNC symbols, 2026.1 release) in the reference store - same identifier space as the counts, so no mapping is needed - via gseapy.prerank as the fgsea equivalent under the Python-only constraint; (5) an integrated report carrying the fit diagnostics (MA, dispersion, p-value histogram), both unshrunken and shrunken effect sizes, the sensitivity verdict, hallmark leading edges, and the reproducibility record, with the edgeR two-method cross-check and transcript-length offsets recorded as stated limitations of the Python-only, gene-level setup.
